verdicts.title: compute_loss_func (and label_smoothing_factor) are silently ignored on the default eval path, so eval_loss and best-model selection measure a different objective than training
verdicts.reasoning: Verified every link by reading the file. _dp_trainer.py:2484-2488 gates the per-example eval path on `"loss" in (self.args.include_for_metrics or [])`; _training_arguments.py:364 declares `include_for_metrics: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)`, so the gate is off by default. The default branch (2556-2572) forwards only `{**model_inputs, **labels_kwargs}` to the model and reads `output.get("loss")`. `grep -n _compute_loss_func` returns only 467, 2320, 2322 - it is never consulted on that branch, and no warning is emitted there (the only nearby warning, 2534-2541, is about logits-only predictions on the *opposite* branch). The label-smoothing half of the claim also holds: `label_smoothing` is injected into inputs only at 2300-2308 inside compute_per_example_loss, and the trainer-side F.cross_entropy rebuild lives at 2333-2357 in the same method, so neither runs on the batched eval path. Divergence from upstream confirmed against the installed transformers 5.15.1: `Trainer.prediction_step` routes through `self.compute_loss(...)`, which applies compute_loss_func / the label smoother. No test pins the batched-eval behaviour w.r.t. compute_loss_func (the only compute_loss_func tests are SFT-side, test_trl_trainers.py:416/451/1295). No user-facing doc mentions the eval exclusion - docs/user-guide/huggingface/dptrainer.md:127 and docs/reference/transformers.md:58 describe the hook without it; the only mention is the source comment at 2550-2555. Mitigating (why not high): Opaque's compute_loss_func has a per-example-under-vmap contract, so it *cannot* be applied verbatim to a batched forward - the design constraint is real and there is a working opt-in - and nothing here touches privacy or the trained weights. Kept at medium because the divergence is silent and steers load_best_model_at_end / early stopping.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With the default `include_for_metrics=[]`, DPTrainer.prediction_step takes the batched branch and reports the model's own loss. A user who passes `compute_loss_func=my_weighted_ce` (or sets `label_smoothing_factor>0`) trains against that objective but gets `eval_loss` computed from the HF model's built-in `ForCausalLMLoss` with no smoothing and no warning, so `metric_for_best_model='eval_loss'`, `load_best_model_at_end=True`, early-stopping callbacks and logged eval curves are all driven by an objective the user did not select. Upstream `transformers.Trainer.prediction_step` (5.15.1) routes through `compute_loss` and does apply both. The opt-in exists (`include_for_metrics=['loss']`) but is documented only in a source comment. No effect on training, on the released model's privacy, or on epsilon.

verdicts.title: set_discretization is a full replace, not a partial update: tuning one knob reverts every previously tightened Monte Carlo / grid parameter to the library default
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly on the current tree with `uv run python`: start -> mc_resolution=1e-05, mc_failure_probability=1e-06; after `set_discretization(mc_failure_probability=1e-10, mc_resolution=1e-8)` -> 1e-08 / 1e-10; after `set_discretization(discretization=1e-3)` -> discretization=0.001 with mc_resolution back to 1e-05 and mc_failure_probability back to 1e-06. The code at discretization.py:144-154 constructs `DiscretizationConfig(...)` purely from its arguments and never reads the existing `_default_config`, and the docstring's own worked example (132-133) is the single-knob call shape. Counter-arguments I weighed and why they do not refute: (a) the signature carries explicit literal defaults, so a careful reader can infer full-replace semantics - but the docstring says 'Set module-level default discretization parameters' and never says omitted parameters reset, and `get_discretization` is deliberately keyword-only with `None` sentinels (147-166), i.e. the sibling function *is* an override, which is exactly the asymmetry the reporter flags; (b) the effect is confined to a process that calls the setter twice - it is a footgun, not a wrong formula, and nothing on the default path is affected. Downgraded to low on that basis: no mechanism, sampler or PLD kernel is wrong; only a user-configured tightening is silently undone. affects_epsilon left true because mc_resolution / mc_failure_probability and discretization all move the reported number in the *non*-conservative direction (looser certification) after the second call.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: In a single process, `acc.set_discretization(mc_failure_probability=1e-10, mc_resolution=1e-8)` followed later (e.g. from a shared setup module) by `acc.set_discretization(discretization=1e-3)` leaves the config at discretization=1e-3, mc_resolution=1e-05, mc_failure_probability=1e-06 - both Monte Carlo band parameters silently back at the library defaults, four orders of magnitude looser on the failure probability. Every epsilon computed afterwards by the Monte Carlo accountants (b-min-sep, balls-in-bins) is certified at a weaker confidence level than configured, with no warning. Requires two calls to the setter in one process; single-call and default usage are unaffected.

verdicts.title: is_runtime_patched() returns True even when zero runtime patches were installed
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanical half of the claim is accurate (patches/__init__.py:101-102 sets `_runtime_patches_applied = True` before any patch; the masking/moe/collator installs are wrapped in `except ImportError: pass` at 110-137), but the failure chain does not hold. (1) The predicate's own docstring (152-158) defines it as '``True`` once :func:`apply_runtime_patches` has run in this interpreter' - that is precisely what it returns, so it does not fail open against its documented contract. (2) I ran the reporter's realistic scenario - blocking only the third-party `transformers` and `peft` imports - and `import opaque.patches` still succeeds, `apply_runtime_patches()` runs, and the torch-side gradient-checkpointing patch *is* installed: `opaque.api.patches.torch.is_checkpoint_patched() -> True`, with logs 'transformers not importable; HuggingFace checkpoint glue skipped. The torch-side checkpoint+vmap composition does not depend on it.' and 'applied checkpoint+functorch compatibility patches.' So the claimed 'zero patches installed' state does not occur in a transformers-free install, and in that install the three swallowed patches are moot because there are no HF primitives to drive. (3) The reporter's repro achieved 'zero patches' only by monkeypatching `builtins.__import__` to block Opaque's *own* modules including `opaque.api.patches.torch` - a state no installation can produce. (4) Their supporting evidence is invalid independently: I confirmed that even on a fully successful patch, `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint.__module__` stays 'torch.utils.checkpoint', so that check never demonstrates 'unpatched'. (5) The remaining theoretical path - transformers present but a version whose module layout breaks - is also weak: apply_masking_patches (masking.py:313-352) itself swallows ImportError and uses `hasattr` guards, so version drift is absorbed inside, not by the outer handler.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No demonstrated failure. With transformers/peft absent, `apply_runtime_patches()` still installs the torch-side checkpoint+functorch shim (verified: is_checkpoint_patched() -> True) and logs why the HF glue was skipped, and no HF primitives exist to be driven unsafely. `is_runtime_patched()` returns exactly what its docstring promises - that apply_runtime_patches has run. The only residual, cosmetic, improvement is that the three transformers-side installs at __init__.py:110-137 swallow ImportError without a debug log, unlike the checkpoint branch which logs.

verdicts.title: BandMfStrategy drops min_sep / max_participations into a **_ kwargs sink
verdicts.reasoning: The observation is accurate (_band_mf.py:112/125/128 use `**_`, and `.sensitivity(n_steps=1000, min_sep=1, max_participations=1000)` equals `.sensitivity(n_steps=1000)`), but ignoring those two arguments is the *correct* behaviour here, not a defect. For BandMF the participation model is carried by the amplifier, not by the strategy: (a) CyclicPoisson encodes it as `atomic_unit = strategy.bands` and `num_groups = ceil(rounded/bands)` (_poisson.py:70-84, 180-190) - with b bands and b-cyclic participation, a user's participation columns occupy disjoint row blocks [j, j+b) and [j+b, j+2b), so the mechanism factors into ceil(n/b) independent Poisson-Gaussian steps each of sensitivity = the single column norm, which is exactly what `coefs.norm()` and the `num_groups` self-composition implement; (b) BMinSep passes coefs + the min-sep participation structure into the Rust kernels `bandmf_b_min_sep_pld_from_transcript_handle` / `bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld` (_b_min_sep/__init__.py:169-212) and uses `sensitivity` only to rescale the noise multiplier. Crucially, CyclicPoisson.min_sep is a *documented degenerate placeholder* returning 1 (_poisson.py:86-95) - if BandMfStrategy.sensitivity actually consumed it, the result would be wrong, not tighter. So the '**_ sink is the one signal that could have flagged the mismatch' framing is backwards: there is no signal to consume. The genuinely substantive part of the finding - that `poisson()` will happily price a BandMF strategy that the runtime pairs with a plain non-cyclic `opaque.dpsgd.PoissonSampler`, yielding the ~2.9x epsilon reduction - is the sampler/accounting binding problem the reporter themselves attributes to open #320/#356/#359, and it is not a materially worse instance: a correct `CyclicPoissonSampler` does exist and is exported from `opaque.dpftrl.sampling`, so this is the same 'nothing binds sampler to accountant' gap already tracked (#359 names BandMF participation sensitivity specifically).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No new defect. BandMfStrategy.sensitivity correctly returns the single-participation column norm and correctly ignores min_sep/max_participations, because for BandMF the participation structure is applied by the amplifier (CyclicPoisson's num_groups = ceil(n_steps/bands); BMinSep's Rust Monte Carlo transcript) rather than by the strategy, and CyclicPoisson.min_sep is a documented degenerate 1 that would produce a wrong sensitivity if consumed. The residual risk - a user hand-pairing `ftrl_acc.poisson(mf_gaussian(nm, band_mf_strategy(bands=16)), ...)` with a non-cyclic sampler and getting an epsilon valid only under b-cyclic participation - is the already-tracked sampler-to-accountant binding gap (#320/#356/#359); the correct `CyclicPoissonSampler` is available in `opaque.dpftrl.sampling`.

verdicts.title: The shipped opaque.accounting module docstring names accounting factories that do not exist and omits the ones that do
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py:9-13 lists `gaussian, adaclip, poisson, truncated_poisson, parallel_poisson` for opaque.dpsgd.accounting and `band_mf, blt, bisr, bsr, lambda_cgd, identity_mf, poisson, b_min_sep, balls_in_bins` for opaque.dpftrl.accounting. Runtime check on the current tree: `opaque.dpsgd.accounting.__all__ == ['adaclip','gaussian','k_out_of_t','parallel_poisson','poisson','random_allocation']` with `hasattr(..., 'truncated_poisson') == False`; `opaque.dpftrl.accounting.__all__ == ['b_min_sep','balls_in_bins','mf_gaussian','per_step','poisson']` with all six of band_mf/blt/bisr/bsr/lambda_cgd/identity_mf absent. So six of the nine DP-FTRL names and one of the five DP-SGD names are wrong, `mf_gaussian` (the single factory that actually instantiates every MF mechanism) is unmentioned, and `k_out_of_t` / `random_allocation` / `per_step` are undocumented here. This is the shipped source docstring rendered by help() and the API reference, a separate file from the docs/ drift the reporter says was reported elsewhere. Severity low: failure is a loud AttributeError, no numerical or privacy consequence - pure discovery friction. Not folded into #324 ('Make documentation and published claims mechanically verifiable'), which is a process/CI issue rather than this concrete stale docstring. Noted in passing while verifying: the `poisson()` docstring in packages/opaque-dpftrl/.../amplification/_poisson.py:280-283 has the same class of drift (`band_mf_strategy(n_steps=1000, bands=10)` - the factory has no `n_steps` parameter).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user reading `help(opaque.accounting)` or the generated reference follows the docstring and writes `import opaque.dpftrl.accounting as ftrl_acc; ftrl_acc.blt(nm, ...)`, getting `AttributeError: module 'opaque.dpftrl.accounting' has no attribute 'blt'` with no pointer to the real entry point `ftrl_acc.mf_gaussian(nm, blt_strategy(...))`. Same for band_mf, bisr, bsr, lambda_cgd, identity_mf and for `opaque.dpsgd.accounting.truncated_poisson`. The failure is loud and immediate, so the cost is discovery friction only - no wrong epsilon, no silent misconfiguration.

verdicts.title: build_strategy silently discards privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs for mf_identity while every other mechanism raises TypeError on an unknown key
verdicts.reasoning: Verified by reading. _dpftrl.py:108-118: `factory = _STRATEGY_FACTORIES[mechanism]; if mechanism == "mf_identity": return factory(); extra = dict(kwargs) if kwargs else {}; ...; return factory(**extra)`. `identity_strategy()` (_identity.py:49-51) takes no parameters, so without the short-circuit any leftover key would raise TypeError, matching the other five mechanisms. The branch is not needed for anything else: `_MECH_DEFAULTS['mf_identity'] = {}` (_training_arguments.py:213) pre-merges nothing, and `_LR_SCHEDULED_STRATEGIES` is `{'mf_band','mf_blt'}` so no lr_schedule is auto-injected for mf_identity either - the branch is pure kwargs-dropping. I also confirmed there is no upstream key validator: `__post_init__` (1078-1081) only `setdefault`s per-mechanism defaults into privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs, and the only key rejection nearby (1084-1094) targets `sampling_kwargs`, not mechanism kwargs. Severity reduced to low and the reporter's framing narrowed: the user explicitly selected `mf_identity`, so 'the user believes they are still running a banded mechanism' overstates it - the concrete harm is only that a stale/mistyped key is dropped without complaint where five sibling mechanisms would have raised. affects_epsilon is correctly false: strategy and accountant both use IdentityStrategy, so noise and accounting stay consistent.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With `privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_identity'`, any content of `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs` (e.g. a leftover `{'bands': 8}` from an earlier mf_band config, or a typo'd key) is dropped at _dpftrl.py:109-110 with no error and no warning, while the same stale or mistyped key under mf_band / mf_blt / mf_bisr / mf_bsr / mf_lambda_cgd surfaces as a TypeError from the strategy factory at line 118. No upstream validator rejects unknown mechanism-kwargs keys. The run proceeds with the plain identity strategy, and since the accountant is built from the same strategy object the reported epsilon stays consistent - the cost is a silently ignored configuration knob and an asymmetric error surface when switching mechanism strings.
